Here's a description of the provided plot, following the guidelines:

The plot illustrates the relationship between the number of iterations and the loss value for different Large Language Models (LLMs). The x-axis is labeled “#Iteration” and has a linear scale ranging from 0 to 140000, with tick labels spaced every 20000 units. The y-axis is labeled “Loss” and has a linear scale ranging from 2.4 to 3.4, with tick labels spaced every 0.1 units. A purple line represents “Vanilla”, starting at approximately 3.3 at an iteration of 0 and decreasing to approximately 2.5 at an iteration of 140000, with a steep decline in the first 20000 iterations. An orange line represents “StrmLLM (n=64)”, beginning at approximately 3.2 at an iteration of 0 and decreasing to approximately 2.5 at an iteration of 140000, also with a steep decline in the first 20000 iterations. A green line represents “SepLLM (n=64)”, starting at approximately 3.1 at an iteration of 0 and decreasing to approximately 2.5 at an iteration of 140000, with a similar initial decline. A maroon line represents “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)”, beginning at approximately 3.0 at an iteration of 0 and decreasing to approximately 2.5 at an iteration of 140000, showing a similar trend. Finally, a navy blue line represents “SepLLM (n=128)”, starting at approximately 3.3 at an iteration of 0 and decreasing to approximately 2.5 at an iteration of 140000, with a similar initial decline.
